original_card.question: Can one specified masked or overcomplete decoder improve the complete moment budget?
methods: Synthesize a decoder with exact coefficients and fully priced helper endpoints.
Bound the best possible budget for a fixed support alphabet before synthesis.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound and count all copied information, frames and restoration.

first_step.inspect: Locate the excluded classes: masked identities, at least nine terms, and deeper punctures.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Choose one finite support alphabet and test exact decoding constraints before building a whole network.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A cheaper fully realized decoder could increase deficit or lower recursive cost on the binding complex side.
allowed_variations: Select a specific masked or overcomplete family with exact labels and supports.
scope_change_triggers: Repeating the exact eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.

actual_scope: Proof obligation inside the masked (E-graph) model: is every rank-<=8 solution of PR1212's system (E) on P112 minus X, for every 4-subset X not inside a P112 frame (the part of P108 that PR1419's extension lemma cannot reach; 168 orbits), equal to D(2G)D^-1, so that decoders with exactly eight costly terms keep PR968's floor 60 on every P108 unit?
scope_change_reason: The card asks whether a masked decoder can beat the floor. PR1212/PR1389/PR1399 answered it for exactly eight costly terms on P120, P112, P111 and every P104 frame complement, PR1419 for punctures inside a frame, PR1425 for the rest of P110 and the P109 package (PR1469) for the rest of P109, whose open next question is P108. This closes it; it does not construct a decoder.
bottleneck_link: Side result on the binding complex supplier: masked eight-costly-term decoders cannot beat PR968's floor on any P108 unit, so the remaining masked escape routes are nine or more costly terms or punctures of depth five or more not inside a frame.
stop_rule: Stop at P108 with one PR; P107 and deeper (orbit counts growing toward order 1e5 at P105), and nine or more costly terms, are left as handoffs.
evidence: verify.py: 174 exact checks in about 2.5 minutes (generators; triple orbits; a candidate-lemma coverage argument with explicit generator words for all 2468 open candidates; per unit (168) the pivot's D4 structure, (I3), (I4) and gluing, Lemma 9 connectivity and algebra, assembly, CNF consistency, DRUP replay of zero exclusion with its own RUP checker and the needs-zero-clause control; one bogus-proof control). The 180-orbit quadruple census (168 open) matches an independently written census by OpenAI Codex (recorded, not needed by the argument); a read-only adversarial review by OpenAI Codex found no soundness gap (not a human review).
author: JosieElliston (with Claude Opus 5.5 via Claude Code)
ai_assistance: Claude Opus 5.5 via Claude Code: proof, coverage argument, verifier and write-up. OpenAI Codex: independent orbit census from a specification and a read-only adversarial review. Submitted by the account holder.

open_questions.question: Does rank-8 rigidity of (E) hold on P107-P105 units (P112 minus 5-7 lines not inside a P112 frame), and can the per-orbit DRUP step (I2) be replaced by a structural zero-exclusion lemma?
open_questions.why_it_matters: PR968's floor covers punctures up to p = 15 (P105); with PR1419's Lemma 10, rigidity of every P105 unit would give every intermediate depth at once. Per-orbit certificates already cost about 6 MB at P108 and P105 has on the order of 1e5 orbits.
open_questions.first_step: Run make_proof.py's pivot rule and CNF on P107 candidates (P108 orbit representative + one line) to measure proof volume; separately, look for a pivot-local argument that excludes zeros using only the trans and diag families, which carry most refutations.
open_questions.blocked_by: Proof volume grows with the orbit count; no structural replacement for (I2) is known.
